claims.statement: Workspace Navigator preserves native SwiftUI List row dragging: macOS 26 and later use draggable with drag state set only when the List session becomes active, while older systems use onDrag and have no Workspace tear-off completion observer.

Workspace layout receivers are pre-mounted native overlays that read current window payload and target eligibility during drag callbacks, require a matching pasteboard UUID, and pass ordinary pointer events through even when stale drag state exists.

Navigator translates globally measured row geometry at its native List overlay and clamps pointer positions to Workspace insertion boundaries; preview boundaries include the dragged row while mutation indices exclude it, and switching away from Navigator rejects drops immediately.
Dragging the selected combinable workspace derives a displayed merge target from its immediate next or previous eligible neighbor without committing a selection change.

Pane preview geometry omits the dragged pane while keeping its source view mounted; pane drop mutation precedes clearing drag state to avoid temporarily mounting the same native surface under two parents.

Pane-area layout drops merge another combinable workspace's whole split tree or rearrange an individual pane only within the target workspace; occupied panes choose a proportional nearest edge and empty slots use whole-area replacement, while Navigator pane detachment requires a multi-pane source.

The Pane drag source is attached to eligible title content and starts a native session using a retained mouseDragged event; its transparent background recognizer rejects double-clicks, hidden or clipped sources, text controls and parked panes without delaying ordinary mouse events.

Layout tear-off requires an unaccepted operation, a released primary mouse button, no Escape cancellation, and a release outside the source window; an unhandled release over another window still qualifies, but accepted drops do not create a new window.

Workspace cancellation tracking latches Escape across repeated active callbacks using a local key monitor and common/eventTracking run-loop key-state observation, and releases both observers when tracking ends or deinitializes.

Workspace failed-drop return animation is disabled at native willBegin through a data-source proxy that first calls the original callback and forwards other behavior; the marker rebinds after SwiftUI replacement and restores the original only while its own proxy remains installed.

The native Pane session disables failed-drop return animation at creation and advertises move only inside the application, while macOS 26 Workspace drag configuration also disables external UUID copy.

MainWindowCoordinator deduplicates source/move requests and leaves ownership in the source until native destination registration. Registration consumes a matched request once even if extraction is empty; source close discards pending requests and restored scenes never replay a move.

Whole-workspace transfer preserves the same Workspace and full split layout; split-pane transfer wraps the existing Pane in an automatically named Workspace without inheriting the group name or template identity, while a lone pane carries its original Workspace, name and template identity. Neither extraction disconnects transports, ends history events or adds reopen history. Whole-workspace extraction clears its lifecycle router and destination open assigns the target router; split extraction retains the source workspace router. Both validated extraction entrypoints cancel pending persistent-close requests before ownership removal.

Drag-created windows suppress native opening animation, use the source's ordinary content size, choose the release-point screen and fit a top-centered initial frame within its visible bounds; restored windows without a request keep their system-restored frame.

The pane content drop target is a separate outermost overlay above terminal/table native content and outside the workspace layout receiver; it is enabled only on active supported panes when window layout/conversation drag state is nil. SSH accepts files, SFTP items and terminal paths; SFTP accepts files and SFTP items; Telnet and Serial accept terminal paths only, while empty panes have no content drop target.

Assistant conversation rows use a separate onDrag payload and permit active conversations to move during runs, approvals or compaction; archived rows and rename editors cannot start a drag, search results disable reorder callbacks, and this source has no Workspace/Pane tear-off completion path.

Assistant native insertion resolves live conversation drag state and a string pasteboard type to a Pinned/Chats section plus beforeID using row midpoints and section headers; the native gate does not compare the pasteboard UUID to the live ID.

A retained hidden Assistant list must both unregister native dragged types and return nil from hit testing to avoid stealing drops; recycled hosting rows explicitly receive the owning window, locale and color scheme for native callbacks.

Production Assistant reorder dispatches through WindowModel and AppModel to AssistantConversationOperations, persists normalized pin/order metadata before publishing it and preserves conversation run state; persistence failure leaves visible order unchanged and is reported to the requesting window.

Native Workspace mouse/session regression cases are explicitly gated by requiresVisibleWindow; the split-workspace tear-off test checks one request, animation disabled at session start and transfer of the original Workspace and pane IDs.

Visible-window drag tests are skipped unless the test host has TERMIND_WINDOW_TESTS=1; offscreen Navigator geometry and payload tests run without that opt-in, while the single-click, native mouse-session and split-workspace tear-off tests are gated because they make a window key or activate the app.
In Debug test runs the app suppresses automatic window launch unless TERMIND_WINDOW_TESTS=1 or a screenshot demo is active; this launch safeguard is independent of per-test visible-window gating.

TermindCommands supplies MainWindowCoordinator's scene factory using the UUID-valued main WindowGroup; after the diagnosis-consent gate TermindApp configures a fresh destination model before RootView construction. MainWindowRegistration consumes the move only after native attachment, attaching a forwarding WorkspaceWindowCloseDelegate and establishing full-size content coordinates first. It observes initial and new isDocumentEdited values and clears true values without bypassing native close confirmation. The close proxy honors the forwarded delegate's veto, confirms only for an open model owning workspaces, forwards other supported callbacks, and restores the prior delegate on detachment only if still installed. This leaves registration-time live transfer and stable Workspace/Pane identity and connection/history semantics unchanged. Close-confirmation tests exercise the proxy directly; move tests register directly through the coordinator rather than testing edited-state observation.

A transfer request snapshots ordinary source content size, sidebar presentation and width, fullscreen state and source-screen center; the destination is configured before initial layout and reconfigured at registration, sized, then has its initial sidebar layout generation bumped for any move request, with fullscreen transition deferred until the native window becomes key.

MainWindowCoordinator consumes a move request at most once when a destination's native window registers, and ignores subsequent registration of the same native/model pair rather than transferring the layout twice.

Closing a source window records/disconnects only still-owned workspaces, preserving transferred panes' connections and active history until their destination closes. Persistent-close authorization checks session ownership and workspace/pane snapshots; generation cancellation dismisses pending failure prompts and prevents further authorization but does not undo completed remote termination. SessionPersistenceTests covers cancellation between batch terminations separately from the move tests' ownership/history assertions.
Pane content drops dispatch terminal paths to a terminal owner's paste operation and file or SFTP-item payloads to pane-local upload/copy requests, rather than performing workspace layout moves.
